title: Scalable Hydrodynamics on multiple Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs)
problem: Porting stencil-based hydrodynamic simulations from CPU/GPU architectures to FPGAs is challenging; FPGAs offer energy efficiency but have lower throughput than GPUs for HPC applications
motivation: FPGAs provide customizable hardware and on-chip memory that can be tailored for specific HPC workloads with excellent energy efficiency. However, their viability and performance characteristics for large-scale scientific simulations remain unclear, particularly for multi-FPGA systems.
method: Implementation of 2D and 3D hydrodynamics solvers on Intel Agilex 7 FPGAs using Intel oneAPI framework; optimizations leverage FPGA's large cache for data reuse and memory streaming reduction; domain decomposition enables pipeline duplication and multi-FPGA scaling
key_novelty: First practical demonstration of scalable hydrodynamics simulations on multi-FPGA systems, showing competitive energy efficiency with GPUs despite lower throughput
contributions: Scalable 2D and 3D hydrodynamics solver implementations on FPGAs
Domain decomposition strategy enabling pipeline duplication and multi-card scaling
Memory optimization leveraging FPGA's large on-chip cache for data reuse
Energy efficiency comparable to NVIDIA A100 GPUs
Insights for heterogeneous HPC system design and exascale computing
limitations: Abstract lacks specific throughput and latency numbers; energy efficiency comparison to GPUs only qualitative ('comparable'); scalability beyond 2 FPGAs not discussed
